items.note: A combined Sūrya-Hari-Hara-Pitāmaha image is found at the Udayeśvara temple, Udaypur: eight-armed standing figure with trident, lotus, conch, rosary, varada and cakra.
items.gloss: Besides Harihara, a composite image of Viṣṇu, Śiva and Sūrya has been found in the Udayeśvara temple at Udaypur. It is a standing eight-armed figure with three hands broken; the right hands hold trident, lotus, conch, rosary and the varada pose, and on the left only the hand holding the cakra survives.

items.note: This composite image has all the characteristics described in the 'Aparājitapṛcchā'; main deity Sūrya, with Śiva, Viṣṇu and Brahmā attributes; may be called Sūrya-Hari-Hara-Pitāmaha.
items.gloss: All the characteristics of this composite image, described in the Aparājitapṛcchā (213, 32-34), are present in it. The main deity is Sūrya; the trident is Śiva's, lotus and conch are Viṣṇu's and the rosary is Brahmā's. The image may be called Sūrya-Hari-Hara-Pitāmaha.

items.note: Study shows composite images held a considerably important place in the Paramāra period.
items.gloss: From the above study it is clear that composite images were given a very important place in the Paramāra period.

items.gloss: At this time the Chandellas in the Bundelkhand region, the Kalachuris, the Kachchhapaghātas in the Gwalior region and the Paramāras in Mālwā ... these contemporary dynasties set unparalleled standards in military art, literature, architecture and sculpture.

items.note: Rivalry among regional dynasties in temple building left the region full of fine temples, of which only traces survive.
items.gloss: These contemporary dynasties set unparalleled standards in military art, literature, architecture and sculpture. Rivalry in temple building went on among them, so that at one time the region was filled with excellent and incomparable temples, but now only a trace of them remains.

items.note: Paramāra rulers' contribution to temple architecture; Bhoja's Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra gives detailed knowledge of architecture, painting and iconography.
items.gloss: The Paramāra rulers of Mālwā made an important contribution to temple architecture. In the evaluation of this dynasty its work 'Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra' holds an important place. This work gives extensive information on architecture, painting and iconography.

items.note: Distinctive feature of the Paramāra style is the Bhūmija śikhara with four spines and miniature shrine forms between them, and a prominent sukanāsa panel.
items.gloss: The distinguishing feature of the Paramāra style in temple architecture is the Bhūmija-type śikhara. It has four spines decorated with a mesh of jāla, while the quadrants between the spines are filled with small shrine forms, arranged in rows of diminishing height. Another feature of Paramāra temples is the prominent sukanāsa panel with an image slab inside a sloping chaitya-arch and at the base of each spine.

claim.value: Bhūmija-type śikhara described as the distinctive feature of the Paramāra style

items.note: Paramāra temples: pillars richly ornamented, plan on a square axis, garbhagṛha, antarāla and pillared maṇḍapa, normally no pradakṣiṇāpatha; OCR damaged.
items.gloss: The pillars are low and highly ornamented; most temples are planned on a square axis. Temples of this group include a garbhagṛha, antarāla and a pillared maṇḍapa. As a rule they do not include a circumambulatory path (pradakṣiṇāpatha).
